Case Study

Osteoarthritis Care Plan

Recommending Evidence-Based Alternatives to Knee Surgery

Role
Senior UX/UI Designer
Type
Professional Work
Company
Optum Technology
Tools
Figma Design · Figma Make · Copilot · Jira · Miro · Userview

A provider reviewing the OA Care Digital recommendation on their laptop during a patient visit

Overview

The Challenge

25% of total knee and hip replacement surgeries result in patients not feeling better after 6 months compared to their pre-surgery state. Despite this, the clinical tools available to providers offered little guidance on evidence-based non-surgical alternatives before reaching the operating table.

This project extended an existing suite of medication recommenders, already serving complex patients across 7 disease states including CHF, T2DM, HFrEF, and Hypertension, into a new domain: Osteoarthritis. Specifically its care pathway guidance embedded directly inside the EHR.

Product Users

Anyone who relies on digital tools to manage knee pain patients, recommend treatment options, and make informed care decisions, including primary care physicians, orthopedic surgeons, and clinical staff supporting the decision-making process.

Problem Statement

How Might We

How might we design a care pathway recommender that helps primary care physicians and orthopedic surgeons recommend evidence-based alternatives to knee surgery, enabling patients to achieve better long-term outcomes?

Objectives & Goals

01

Alert providers to medication optimization opportunities based on the patient's insurance formulary

02

Identify patients viable for conservative care plan programs before surgery is considered

03

Visualize predicted long-term improvement across surgical and non-surgical care paths

04

Surface recommendations within the existing EHR workflow without disrupting clinical routines

05

Support shared decision-making between specialists and patients at the point of care

Constraints

Working Inside the Requirements

The recommendation had to live inside an existing, highly regulated EHR workflow without adding annoying clicks during an already time-constrained patient visit. Every decision also had to fit within Optum's existing design system and clear clinical and compliance reviews before it could ship.

Process

How We Worked

The project operated within a large, cross-functional scrum team. Provider interviews were conducted at project initiation to gather business requirements and understand intended clinical workflows, forming the foundation for all subsequent design decisions.

Research

Business Challenges

01

High surgical failure rate, 25% of knee and hip replacements leave patients no better off after 6 months, creating both a clinical and cost burden

02

Providers lacked a unified tool to evaluate non-surgical care pathways alongside surgical options at the point of care

03

Existing medication recommenders were siloed by disease state, with no pathway for musculoskeletal or surgical care guidance

04

Insurance formulary complexity made it difficult for providers to quickly determine which medication alternatives were covered for each patient

05

Limited research funding required the team to rely on internal provider interviews rather than formal usability studies

06

EHR integration constraints demanded a widget-based approach that fit naturally into existing provider workflows without a separate product login

Design

The Product

The result is an EHR-embedded widget that surfaces contextual care opportunities for osteoarthritis patients, pulling directly from the patient's existing record to generate relevant, actionable recommendations without requiring providers to leave their workflow.

Primary Landing Page After Clicking the EHR Alert. Care Strategy view inside the EHR visit workflow, showing the OA Care Digital recommendation alongside predicted improvement, complication risk, and rationale

Features included

01
Medication Opportunity Alerts
Surfaces recommendations to discontinue or switch medications based on the patient's current insurance formulary, reducing out-of-pocket cost and improving adherence.
02
Care Plan Viability Screening
Identifies patients who qualify for conservative, non-surgical care programs and prompts providers to initiate enrollment, helping defer or avoid unnecessary procedures.
03
Surgical Outcome Projections
Displays predicted improvement graphs by care path, enabling specialists and patients to make informed, side-by-side comparisons of surgical versus non-surgical trajectories.

Recommender Landing Menu. A mockup of the recommender's landing menu page, showing OA Care Digital surfaced as a Next Best Action alongside care opportunities across every disease state, giving providers a holistic view of the patient

A referrals tool embedded directly in the recommender, letting providers order physical therapy without leaving the workflow. Keeping referrals this close to the recommendation is critical, every extra step or app switch is a chance for a provider to lose momentum and the patient to fall through the cracks

Trade-offs

Alternatives Considered

01

A standalone dashboard, or an embedded recommendation?

We considered a standalone dashboard for comparing care paths, but chose to embed recommendations directly into the existing EHR table instead. That avoided adding a new workflow step, though it limited how much predictive detail we could show at a glance.

02

Surface it for everyone, or just likely candidates?

We considered surfacing conservative care alternatives for every patient, but chose to limit it to likely candidates only. That reduced alert fatigue for providers, accepting some under surfacing at the edges.

03

Flexibility, or auditability?

We considered giving providers a free text override for the recommendation, but chose a constrained set of options instead. That supported auditability and compliance, at the cost of some clinical flexibility.

Design Artifacts

Design Evolution

The OA recommender didn't start as its own product. Early rapid prototypes explored combining osteoarthritis guidance with the team's existing heart failure and diabetes pathways into a single unified recommender, before we split OA into a focused, standalone widget.

From Siloed Tool to Combined Prototype to Focused Product
